cumbia-percussion.title: Cumbia: the percussionist ukulele
cumbia-percussion.description: Imitate the band's percussion with your strumming hand: the kick drum with your thumb, the conga slap with a chuck, the guiro's "chaa-k-k" in 16th notes. At each step, you mute the instrument you're imitating and take its place.

cumbiaperc-01-grosse-caisse.title: Your thumb is the kick drum
cumbiaperc-01-grosse-caisse.description: The cumbia kick drum hits on 1 and 3. It's muted: your thumb replaces it, on the low strings. Am7 needs no left-hand fingers at all, so all your attention goes to your strumming hand.
cumbiaperc-01-grosse-caisse.goal: A steady thumb on 1 and 3, 2 loops at 90 bpm.
tips: P = thumb on the C and G strings, with weight, like a foot on the kick pedal.
Your thumb lands together with the band's bass: listen to it.
Click "kick" to bring the kick drum back and check you land together, then mute it again.

cumbiaperc-02-claque.title: Your chuck is the conga slap
cumbiaperc-02-claque.description: On 2 and 4, the conga player plays a "slap", a dry, high sound. On ukulele, that's the chuck: your palm drops onto the strings as you strum. Still a single voice: only the slaps.
cumbiaperc-02-claque.goal: Your chucks right with the conga slap, 2 loops at 90 bpm.
tips: Find the conga lane in "The band": the slap is the step that lights up on 2 and 4.
Between two slaps, let your hand swing in time without touching the strings.
Say ". CHAK . CHAK" while you play.

cumbiaperc-03-va-et-vient.title: The hand that never stops
cumbiaperc-03-va-et-vient.description: To play like a percussionist, your strumming hand must move in 16th notes without ever stopping: down-up-down-up, four motions per beat. Here you hit all the strings, accenting the down on each beat. This is the engine for the following exercises.
cumbiaperc-03-va-et-vient.goal: Sixteen even strokes per bar, 2 loops at 85 bpm.
tips: Tiny motions from the wrist, hand right next to the strings.
Only the first stroke of each beat is loud: "ONE-e-&-a, TWO-e-&-a".
16th notes go fast: stay at 55-65 bpm as long as your hand tenses up.

cumbiaperc-04-guiro.title: The guiro: chaa-k-k
cumbiaperc-04-guiro.description: The guiro (the guacharaca) plays one long scrape then two short ones on every beat. Your hand keeps its 16th-note back-and-forth, but skips the second step: a loud down, an empty step, then a light down and up.
cumbiaperc-04-guiro.goal: The "long-short-short" aligned with the guiro, 2 loops at 90 bpm.
tips: The empty step is an upstroke that misses the strings: your hand keeps moving.
Compare your grid with the band's guiro lane: they match step by step.
Say "CHAA-k-k" on every beat.

cumbiaperc-05-remplacer-guiro.title: Taking the guiro's place
cumbiaperc-05-remplacer-guiro.description: Same pattern, but the guiro is muted and the guide fades after 2 loops: you are the band's guiro. If you stop, you hear it straight away: the cumbia loses its engine.
cumbiaperc-05-remplacer-guiro.goal: Hold the guiro alone, guide off, 2 loops at 95 bpm.
tips: Listen to the conga and the bass: they're your landmarks now.
Keep exactly the same volume all the way through: a guiro never gets tired.
Bring the guiro back (click "guiro") to check, then mute it again.

cumbiaperc-06-kick-guiro.title: Two voices: kick drum and guiro
cumbiaperc-06-kick-guiro.description: You combine two instruments: on 1 and 3, the guiro's long stroke becomes a thumb stroke (the kick drum); on 2 and 4, it stays a strummed down. The guiro's two light strokes don't change. The kick drum is muted.
cumbiaperc-06-kick-guiro.goal: Thumb and guiro well locked together, 2 loops at 95 bpm.
tips: Your thumb hits lower, on the low strings; your fingers strum all the strings: two motions, one hand.
"BOOM-k-k CHAA-k-k BOOM-k-k CHAA-k-k".
If you stumble, go back to "The guiro: chaa-k-k" and replace only beat 1 with P.

cumbiaperc-07-conga.title: The conga on ukulele
cumbiaperc-07-conga.description: The conga tumbao: a muted stroke on the beat, an open note on the "&", a slap on 2 and 4. On ukulele: light chuck, up, strong chuck, up… and two quick ups at the end to push forward. The conga is muted: you replace it.
cumbiaperc-07-conga.goal: The full tumbao, 2 loops at 95 bpm.
tips: x = light chuck ("too"), X = strong chuck ("CHAK"), u = open upstroke ("ta").
Say "too-ta-CHAK-ta too-ta-CHAK-tata".
The two ups at the end are a little push: they pull you into the next bar.

cumbiaperc-08-trois-voix.title: Three voices: bass, guiro and slap
cumbiaperc-08-trois-voix.description: The full percussionist-ukulele pattern: thumb on 1 and 3 (kick drum), chuck on 2 and 4 (conga slap), and the guiro's little strokes in between. Kick drum and guiro are muted: you play the whole rhythm section.
cumbiaperc-08-trois-voix.goal: The three-voice pattern, 2 loops at 95 bpm.
tips: "BOOM-k-k CHAK-k-k": it's the pattern from exercise 6, with a chuck instead of the down on 2 and 4.
The little strokes stay light: they're what gives the impression of speed.
Listen to what's left of the band (bass, conga): your pattern should complete it exactly.

cumbiaperc-09-accords.title: Percussive rhythm with chords
cumbiaperc-09-accords.description: Your left hand joins in: the three-voice pattern, over C and G7. The chucks help a lot: they leave a split second where your left hand can move without it being heard.
cumbiaperc-09-accords.goal: The pattern without a hitch through the changes, 2 loops at 95 bpm.
tips: Change chords on the last two little strokes of the bar: they're light and forgive everything.
The thumb on beat 1 must land on the new chord: it's what makes the change heard.
C → G7: your ring finger leaves the A string, and the three G7 fingers land together.

cumbiaperc-10-tempo-bal.title: Alone with the bass, at dance-hall tempo
cumbiaperc-10-tempo-bal.description: The final challenge: the Andalusian progression (Am, G, F, E7), with kick drum, guiro and conga muted, the guide fading after 2 loops, and one bar in four with nobody at all. Only the bass and you are left: your ukulele is the whole rhythm section.
cumbiaperc-10-tempo-bal.goal: Hold 2 loops at 100 bpm, guide off.
tips: During the silences, your foot and your voice ("BOOM-k-k CHAK-k-k") are the metronome.
If one hand gets lost, keep the other going: the thumb on 1 and 3 must never drop out.
Your record is saved: a few more bpm each session.
